en: Points of Controversy The Great Fifty The Fourth Chapter
Another discussion on being possessed [of fruits]:
Is a person who is practicing for the realization of Arahantship possessed of three fruits? Yes.
Is a person practicing for the realization of arahantship endowed with four types of contact, four types of feeling, four types of perception,
four types of volition, four types of consciousness, four types of faith, four types of energy, four types of mindfulness,
four types of concentration, and four types of wisdom?
It should not be said thus … [as before] … Is a person practicing for the realization of the fruit of non-returning endowed with two fruits?
Yes.

Is it to be said that a person practicing for the realization of the fruit of non-returning (anāgāmiphala) is endowed with three types of contact, three types of feeling …pe… and three types of wisdom?
Certainly not; such should not be said …pe….
Is a person practicing for the realization of the fruit of once-returning endowed with the fruit of stream-entry?
Yes. Is a person practicing for the realization of the fruit of once-returning endowed with two types of contact and two types of feeling? ... [and so on] ... Yes.
"Is one endowed with two kinds of wisdom?
"One should not say so... [and so on].
"Is a person practicing for the realization of Arahatship endowed with the fruit of Stream-entry? [One should not say so.]
“Yes,” [you say].
“Is a person practicing for the realization of arahantship a stream-enterer who is ‘one who has seven births at most,’ ‘one who goes from family to family,’ or ‘one who has only one seed remaining’?
You should not speak thus… [and so on].
Is a person practicing for the realization of Arahatship endowed with the fruit of a Once-returner?
Yes. Is a person practicing for the realization of Arahatship a Once-returner?
It should not be said thus ...
[and so on] ... Is a person practicing for the realization of Arahatship endowed with the fruit of Non-returning? Yes.

Is a person practicing for the realization of Arahantship—namely, a non-returner who attains Nibbāna in the interval, one who attains Nibbāna upon arrival, one who attains Nibbāna without exertion, one who attains Nibbāna with exertion, or one who goes upstream to the Akaniṭṭha realm—[to be considered] such?
One should not say so… [and so on].
Is a person practicing for the realization of the fruit of Non-returning endowed with the fruit of Stream-entry?
“Yes,” [you say].

“Then should it not be said that a person practicing for the realization of the fruit of non-returning is a stream-enterer who is ‘one who returns seven times at most,’ ‘one who goes from family to family,’ or ‘one who has only one seed remaining’?
Certainly not; such should not be said … [and so on] …
Is a person practicing for the realization of the fruit of non-returning (anāgāmiphala) endowed with the fruit of once-returning (sakadāgāmiphala)?
Yes. Is a person practicing for the realization of the fruit of non-returning a once-returner? No.
It should not be said thus ... [as before] ...
Is a person practicing for the realization of the fruit of once-returning endowed with the fruit of stream-entry?
Yes.

Is a person practicing for the realization of the fruit of once-returning (sakadāgāmiphala) a stream-enterer (sotāpanna) who is "one who has seven births at most," "one who goes from family to family" (kolaṅkolo), or "one who has only one seed remaining" (ekabījī)?
One should not say so... [etc. ...
Is one who possesses the fruit of stream-entry to be called a "stream-enterer"?
“Yes.
“Then is a person who is practicing for the realization of arahantship endowed with the fruit of stream-entry?
“Yes.”
Is that very person who is practicing for the realization of Arahatship a stream-enterer?
One should not say so… [and so on] … Is one who possesses the fruit of a once-returner to be called a “once-returner”?
“Yes.
“Then does a person who is practicing for the realization of arahantship possess the fruit of a once-returner?
“Yes.”
Is that very person who is practicing for the realization of Arahatship a "once-returner"?
One should not say so... [and so forth] ...
Is one who is endowed with the fruit of Non-returning to be called a "non-returner"?
“Yes.
“Is a person who is practicing for the realization of arahantship endowed with the fruit of non-returning?
“Yes.”
That very person who is practicing for the realization of Arahatship— is that person an Anāgāmin?
One should not say so … [and so on] … Is one who possesses the fruit of Stream-entry to be called a “Stream-enterer”?
“Yes.
“Is a person who is practicing for the realization of the fruit of non-returning endowed with the fruit of stream-entry?
“Yes.”
Is that very person who is practicing for the realization of the fruit of non-returning a stream-enterer?
One should not say so … [and so on] … Is one who possesses the fruit of once-returning to be called a "once-returner"?
“Yes.
“Is a person who is practicing for the realization of the fruit of non-returning endowed with the fruit of once-returning?
“Yes.”
That very person who is practicing for the realization of the fruit of non-returning—should he not be called a once-returner?
One should not say so...
[and so on] ...Is one who is endowed with the fruit of stream-entry to be called a "stream-enterer"?
“Yes.
“Then, is a person who is practicing for the realization of the fruit of once-returning endowed with the fruit of stream-entry?
“Yes.”
Is the person who is practicing for the realization of the fruit of once-returning a stream-enterer?
One should not say so … [and so on] … Is the person who is practicing for the realization of arhatship endowed with the fruit of stream-entry?
“Yes.
“But is it not the case that a person practicing for the realization of Arahatship has transcended the fruit of Stream-entry?
“Yes.”
If a person practicing for the realization of Arahatship has transcended the fruit of Stream-entry,
surely it should not be said that "the person practicing for the realization of Arahatship is possessed of the fruit of Stream-entry.
Since the person practicing for the realization of Arahatship has transcended the fruit of Stream-entry, is he nevertheless possessed of it?
“Yes.
“A person practicing for the realization of arahantship has transcended the path of stream-entry;
they have abandoned personality-belief, doubt, and adherence to rules and observances, as well as the lust, hatred, and delusion that lead to states of deprivation.”
"Has one who has transcended delusion, therefore, come to possess it?
One should not say so... [and so on] ...
"Is a person practicing for the realization of Arhatship possessed of the fruit of a Once-returner? One should not say so.
“Yes.
“Is it not the case that a person practicing for the realization of Arahatship has transcended the fruit of a Once-returner?
“Yes.”
If a person practicing for the realization of Arahatship has transcended the fruit of Once-returning,
surely it should not be said that "the person practicing for the realization of Arahatship is possessed of the fruit of Once-returning.
Since the person practicing for the realization of Arahatship has transcended the fruit of Once-returning, is he therefore possessed of it?
“Yes.

“Then you must not say that a person who is practicing for the realization of Arahantship has transcended the path of the once-returner, and has transcended gross sensual lust and gross ill will, yet is still possessed of them.
… [etc. … You must not say so.
Is a person practicing for the realization of Arahatship endowed with the fruit of Non-returning? Yes.
But is it not the case that a person practicing for the realization of Arahatship has already transcended the fruit of Non-returning?
“Yes.
“If a person practicing for the realization of Arahatship has already transcended the fruit of Non-returning, then surely it should not be said:
‘A person practicing for the realization of Arahatship is endowed with the fruit of Non-returning.’”
Is a person practicing for the realization of Arahantship one who has transcended the fruit of Non-returning and is endowed with it? Yes.

Is a person practicing for the realization of Arahantship one who has transcended the path of Non-returning, transcended residual sensual lust, and transcended residual ill will, and is endowed with them?
It should not be said thus … [as before] … Is a person practicing for the realization of the fruit of non-returning endowed with the fruit of stream-entry?
Yes.
Is it not the case that a person practicing for the realization of the fruit of non-returning has transcended the fruit of stream-entry?
Yes, it is.
If a person practicing for the realization of the fruit of non-returning has indeed transcended the fruit of stream-entry, then surely you should not say: [that he has not].
“Is a person practicing for the realization of the fruit of non-returning endowed with the fruit of stream-entry? [One might say:
“A person practicing for the realization of the fruit of non-returning has transcended the fruit of stream-entry; is he therefore endowed with it?
Yes, he is.
Is a person practicing for the realization of the fruit of non-return (anāgāmiphala) one who has transcended the path of stream-entry (sotāpattimagga),
transcended the view of a self-identity (sakkāyadiṭṭhi) …pe… and transcended the delusion leading to states of deprivation (apāya), yet is still possessed of it?
One should not say so …pe….
Is a person practicing for the realization of the fruit of non-return endowed with the fruit of once-returning?
Yes.
But is it not the case that a person practicing for the realization of the fruit of non-return has transcended the fruit of once-returning?
“Yes.
“If a person who is practicing for the realization of the fruit of non-returning has transcended the fruit of once-returning, then surely it should not be said:
‘A person practicing for the realization of the fruit of non-returning is possessed of the fruit of once-returning.’”
Is a person practicing for the realization of the fruit of non-returning one who has transcended the fruit of once-returning, and is endowed with that? Yes.

Is a person practicing for the realization of the fruit of non-returning one who has transcended the path of once-returning, transcended gross sensual lust, and transcended gross ill-will, and is endowed with those?
It should not be said thus … [as before] … Is a person practicing for the realization of the fruit of once-returning endowed with the fruit of stream-entry?
Yes.
Is it not the case that a person practicing for the realization of the fruit of once-returning has transcended the fruit of stream-entry?
Yes, it is.
If a person practicing for the realization of the fruit of once-returning has indeed transcended the fruit of stream-entry, then certainly you should not say: [that he has not].
“Is a person practicing for the realization of the fruit of once-returning possessed of the fruit of stream-entry? [The opponent replies: “Yes. [The proponent asks:
“Does a person practicing for the realization of the fruit of once-returning transcend the fruit of stream-entry, and is he therefore possessed of it? [The opponent replies:
“Yes.”
Is a person practicing for the realization of the fruit of once-returning one who has transcended the path of stream-entry,
transcended personality-belief … [and so on] … transcended the delusion leading to states of deprivation, and is possessed of those [fetters]?
One should not say so … [and so on].
Is it not to be said that "a person practicing for the realization of arahantship is endowed with three fruits"?
Yes, it is.
Is it not the case that a person practicing for the realization of Arahatship has attained the three fruits and is not deprived of them?
Yes, it is so.
If indeed a person practicing for the realization of Arahatship has attained the three fruits and is not deprived of them, then surely you must admit this.
“A person practicing for the realization of arahantship is endowed with three fruits.
Should it not be said that “a person practicing for the realization of the fruit of non-returning is endowed with two fruits”?
“Yes,” you say.
“But surely, by a person who has entered upon the practice for the realization of the fruit of non-returning, two fruits have been attained, and he has not fallen away from them?
“Yes,” you say.
If a person practicing for the realization of the fruit of non-returning has attained two fruits and is not deprived of them, then indeed it should be said of him:
“The person practicing for the realization of the fruit of non-returning is endowed with two fruits.
But it should not be so said.
“Is a person practicing for the realization of the fruit of once-returning endowed with the fruit of stream-entry?”—
Yes.
But has the fruit of stream-entry not already been attained by that person practicing for the realization of the fruit of once-returning, and is he not still possessed of it?
“Yes.
“If it is true that a person practicing for the realization of the fruit of once-returning has attained the fruit of stream-entry and has not fallen away from it, then indeed it must be said:
‘A person practicing for the realization of the fruit of once-returning is endowed with the fruit of stream-entry.’”

If it is accepted that a person practicing for the realization of Arahantship has attained three fruits and has not fallen away from them, and thus the person practicing for the realization of Arahantship is endowed with those three fruits— then,

if it is accepted that a person practicing for the realization of Arahantship has attained four paths and has not fallen away from them, must it not follow that the person practicing for the realization of Arahantship is endowed with those four paths?

It should not be said thus … [as before] … Is it the case that by a person practicing for the realization of the fruit of non-returning, two fruits have been attained and he has not fallen away from them, such that the person practicing for the realization of the fruit of non-returning is endowed with two fruits?
Yes, it is.

Is it not to be said that a person who is practicing for the realization of the fruit of non-returning has attained three paths and has not fallen away from them, and thus a person practicing for the realization of the fruit of non-returning is endowed with three paths?

One should not say so … [and so on] … Is it not to be said that a person who is practicing for the realization of the fruit of once-returning has attained the fruit of stream-entry and has not fallen away from it, and thus a person practicing for the realization of the fruit of once-returning is endowed with the fruit of stream-entry?
[The opponent says: "Yes.

[The respondent asks: "If it is admitted that a person who has entered upon the practice for the realization of the fruit of once-returning has acquired two paths and has not fallen away from them, then must it not be said that a person practicing for the realization of the fruit of once-returning is endowed with two paths?
[The opponent replies: "One should not say so... [and so on].
The discussion on the possession of other qualities is concluded.
